Thanks Samantha — good questions. Below are Redwood's baseline requirements for an executive offsite with ~45 attendees (mixed senior execs + product/engineering leads). Please use these to update vendor quotes.

Baseline requirements (Redwood):
- Onsite medical: single paramedic on-site during core workshop hours (08:00–20:00). Paramedic should be qualified for senior-population events and carry pediatric/adult emergency meds.
- Ambulance on standby: yes — ambulance on-call with 20 minute or less ETA during workshop hours. We will accept on-site standby (parked) OR guaranteed priority ambulance dispatch from the local provider.
- AED: venue must have a functioning AED on the ground floor; we need its location annotated on the floorplan.
- First-aid kit: vendor to supply a stocked kit for 50 people (see attached med-kit-inventory.pdf for preferred inventory).
- Accessibility & mobility: designate a quiet room for attendees with mobility or medical needs and ensure step-free access to at least two breakout rooms.
- COVID/respiratory: no mandatory testing, but clear guidance to attendees to stay home if symptomatic; provide mask packets on request.
- Emergency contact: I will be Redwood's primary 24/7 contact during travel days. Secondary: Laura Bennett (backup). Provide us with a local phone number for the on-call event manager.

Operational asks for vendor/venue pricing:
1) Cost for paramedic (full day) + whether medic comes with a responder kit.
2) Cost and ETA options for ambulance standby vs on-call.
3) Confirmation of AED location and battery/maintenance date.
4) Any venue constraints for ambulances (access/parking restrictions).

I'll loop in Vivek for any regulatory/compliance paperwork and Grace for onsite ops coordination.

Olga Petrov

Hi all,

Thanks for the overview — I'm attaching a draft med-kit inventory and proposed coverage options after visiting the venue last week. Quick notes:

- For 45 senior attendees a single paramedic plus an advanced first-aider (AM/PM split) is appropriate. Paramedic should carry oxygen, IV fluids, and cardiac monitor if possible.
- Ambulance standby is recommended for exec-level events where we have high age-risk attendees; standby parked onsite reduces transfer time but increases cost by ~£850/day. On-call ambulance with guaranteed <20 min response is an acceptable risk tradeoff if parked standby isn't possible.
- AED: currently on site but battery expiry is 2024 — recommend replacement/maintenance check prior to event.
- Heat stress: schedule water stations and allow for shorter sessions if warm weather (forecast currently 22–26C).
- Medication/allergy handling: we'll provide tagged epi-pens and single-use epinephrine if there are known anaphylaxis cases; please collect allergy list in registration form.

I'm attaching med-kit-inventory.pdf (detailed) and a short local-hospital-summary.docx.

On a related note, I saw an advisory about a localized transit strike potential the week of the event. Venue access times could be affected — recommend we keep a flexible shuttle plan for VIPs.

Best,
